newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says still mulling cut in pork import tariff.
newsitem.headline: Japan says still mulling cut in pork import tariff.

text.p: The Japanese government is still considering cutting import tariffs on foreign pork as a way to lower domestic pork prices, Vice Agriculture Minister Masayuki Takahashi said on Monday.

Japan imposed an emergency tariff on pork imports last July, increasing average import prices by 24 percent. The levy, imposed to protect local producers from an influx of imports, is scheduled to expire at the end of June.
Domestic pork prices have risen sharply since Japan banned imports of pork from Taiwan late last month due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease there.
"We're monitoring domestic pork prices, and may cut the tariff rate on foreign pork if necessary. This would not pose a problem legally," Takahashi told Reuters.
Media reports that had Japan denying it was considering cutting pork import tariffs to curb rising pork prices weighed heavily on the Chicago hog futures market last Friday.

Asked whether Japan would resort to cutting import tariffs on pork within this month, Takahashi said: "I can't say yes or no. What I can say at the moment is that we're carefully monitoring domestic pork prices."
